# xpf Whole-Repository Defensive Audit 178

- **Base commit reviewed:** `33ea184d3ac86cd099072bbe6ae2fc49c25d0318`
- **Output path:** `/tmp/codex-review-178.md`
- **Review mode:** immutable, read-only, whole-tree coverage campaign
- **Focus:** Rust AF_XDP correctness, memory/descriptor ownership, packet semantics, and low-latency invariants, with mandatory whole-repository coverage

## Executive Summary

The campaign reviewed **2,476 / 2,476 tracked source files** across **10 expertise areas and 30 isolated batches**. It produced **123 raw candidates** and retained **81 canonical non-duplicate findings** after global adjudication.

Severity: Critical 0, High 19, Medium 47, Low 15. Confidence: High 80, Medium 1, Low 0.

Every surviving Critical/High was re-opened and independently checked by the coordinator: **19 confirmed, 18 raw High/Critical records merged as duplicates, 1 severity-adjusted, 0 left provisional**.

An independent integrity rerun passed all seven campaign invariants: source partition, manifest coverage, report-path coverage, finding schema/evidence authenticity, per-batch records, source immutability, and raw-extraction parity.

## Duplicate Suppression

The pre-review index covered **118 prior final reports**, **403 normalized findings**, **2306 issue headings**, and **2183 PR headings**.

Global adjudication suppressed **42** same-root records. Explicit decisions:

- `A1-b1-F1` -> `#3048`: Audit 177 already merged the same omitted neighbor delete/reinsert MAC-epoch mutation arms into issue #3048; the new evidence does not change root cause, severity, owner, or fix locus.
- `A1-b1-F2` -> `#1769`: Issue #1769 owns the neighbor resolver generation protocol and bump-before-mutation ordering; initial-dump mutation is an omitted producer arm of that same stale-resolver resurrection invariant and fix locus.
- `A1-b1-F4` -> `#4475`: Issue #4475 introduced the NDP Override anti-poisoning predicate in this exact learn path; making its get-plus-insert composition atomic completes the same neighbor trust invariant rather than creating a separate defect owner.
- `A1-b1-F7` -> `#2979`: Issue #2979 owns reverse-NAT BPF entry leakage during session teardown and introduced this delete helper; ignored syscall failure is an incomplete error arm with the same leaked state, lifecycle owner, and retry fix locus.
- `A1-b3-F1` -> `#3225`: Issue #3225 owns address-family-blind host-inbound service/protocol admission in these match structures; wrong-family ICMP numbers are an omitted protocol arm with the same exposure and family-gating remediation.
- `A1-b3-F2` -> `#2410`: Issue #2410 owns fail-closed forwarding-build validation for out-of-domain VLAN identifiers at VlanId::try_from_snapshot; the missing 4094 upper bound is an incomplete validator condition at the same trust boundary.

#### A1-b1 audit report

##### Scope and method

- Base commit: `33ea184d3ac86cd099072bbe6ae2fc49c25d0318`.
- Detached review worktree: `/tmp/review-wt-codex-178-A1-b1`.
- Reviewer-reported context before source analysis: `pwd` was `/tmp/review-wt-codex-178-A1-b1`; `git rev-parse HEAD` was `33ea184d3ac86cd099072bbe6ae2fc49c25d0318`; the sole write scope was `/tmp/review-work-codex-178/codex-A1-b1.md`.
- Batch: A1-b1, exactly 61 assigned files (52,935 source lines at the frozen base).
- Read first: `/tmp/review-work-codex-178/orientation.md`, `/tmp/review-work-codex-178/dedup-index.md`, `CLAUDE.md`, the repository engineering and architecture documents, `userspace-dp/README.md`, `userspace-dp/src/afxdp/README.md`, and the relevant UMEM, frame, worker, TX, and session design documents.
- Method: read every assigned file; traced XDP metadata and physical frame bounds through parsing, policy/session handling, rewrite/tunnel/neighbor resolution, and TX disposition; reviewed unsafe and FFI contracts, descriptor ownership, atomics, queues, generation guards, cache identities, HA/NAT teardown, allocation/locking/syscall behavior, and adversarial test assertions. Direct reads outside the assignment were limited to callers, callees, types, and lifecycle ordering needed to validate candidates.
- Dedup method: searched the shared index by mechanism, title, issue number, path, and proposed fix locus; inspected local `git log`, `git show`, and `git blame` history for each surviving root.
- Focused commands included `cargo test sharded_neighbor -- --nocapture`, `cargo test dump_batch -- --nocapture`, `cargo test -q ndp_na_override -- --nocapture 2>/dev/null`, `cargo test -q dnat_table_entry -- --nocapture 2>/dev/null`, `cargo test -q cached_descriptor_evicted_only_on_neighbor_mac_change -- --nocapture 2>/dev/null`, `cargo test -q in_lock_epoch_gate -- --nocapture 2>/dev/null`, `cargo test -q 'afxdp::parser::tests' -- --nocapture 2>/dev/null`, `cargo test -q 'afxdp::shared_umem::tests' -- --nocapture 2>/dev/null`, `cargo test -q 'afxdp::mpsc_inbox::tests' -- --nocapture 2>/dev/null`, and `cargo test -q 'afxdp::worker_queue::tests' -- --nocapture 2>/dev/null`, all from the detached worktree's `userspace-dp` crate. An initial `cargo test -p xpf-userspace-dp sharded_neighbor -- --nocapture` from the repository root failed because this repository has no root workspace manifest; it made no source change.
- No live AF_XDP interface, privileged BPF-map, raw-netlink fault injection, cluster, failover, or destructive test was run. Unit tests use invalid descriptors or serialization checks where unprivileged BPF is unavailable, so syscall timing and kernel failure paths were established statically rather than measured live.

The already indexed `codex-review-177` mirror-sidecar defect, #1782 timer-wheel low-rate residual, #2410 integer-narrowing root, #2703 TTL-zero root, #3225 configured-token family scoping, #3360 GRE-acceleration plumbing gap, and #4282 missing lease dehydration were not restated unless the retained defect had a different defective state and effective fix locus.

##### Module-by-module inspection log

Legend: **C/S** = correctness/security; **M/R** = memory, concurrency, integer, and resource safety; **Parity** = completeness relative to documented vSRX/Junos behavior; **Perf** = warmed-path latency; **Mod/tests** = ownership boundary and test assessment. A “sound” result means no new candidate survived contract tracing and corrected dedup adjudication, not a proof that the module is defect-free.

- `userspace-dp/src/filter/compiler.rs` - **C/S:** strict lowering, malformed-address/port constraints, action precedence, flex width/base, and fail-closed behavior were checked; sound here, with the surviving rotation defect downstream. **M/R:** checked conversions and bounded vectors; no unsafe/FFI. **Parity:** supported Junos term predicates and modifiers are represented, while known unsupported leaves are gated/documented. **Perf:** compilation allocations are cold-path only. **Mod/tests:** compiler ownership is cohesive and packet-match tests are broad; no test links flex lowering to config-rotation equality.
- `userspace-dp/src/filter/engine/cache_sensitive.rs` - **C/S:** semantic equality and session revalidation were traced; `A1-b7-01` survives because all six flex fields are omitted. **M/R:** Arc identity/runtime-shape checks are ownership-safe and no unsafe exists. **Parity:** stale PBR routing violates immediate filter-change semantics. **Perf:** comparisons run on snapshot rotation, not per packet. **Mod/tests:** centralized comparator is the right locus, but only malformed address/port equality has direct tests.
- `userspace-dp/src/filter/engine/eval.rs` - **C/S:** ordered terms, next-term modifiers, PBR deferral, count ownership, default actions, v4/v6, and non-routing variants were checked; internally sound, but its intentional PBR deferral completes `A1-b7-01`. **M/R:** borrowed slices and ordinary Rust ownership; no unsafe. **Parity:** terminal and modifier behavior follows documented Junos semantics. **Perf:** linear term walk is established design; no new allocation/lock candidate. **Mod/tests:** variants share matching helpers and have extensive verdict/counter tests; no established-session flex/PBR rotation test.
- `userspace-dp/src/filter/engine/matching.rs` - **C/S:** prefix/port/protocol/DSCP/flags/fragment/ICMP/flex matching, checked offset addition, absent-slice handling, and big-endian extraction were checked; local bounds are sound. **M/R:** slice `get` and `checked_add` avoid OOB/alignment hazards. **Parity:** Layer3/Layer4 flexible ranges are implemented; physical-vs-IP-declared flex bounds are already canonicalized elsewhere. **Perf:** no allocation or lock on match. **Mod/tests:** focused helper is cohesive and short/unsupported-base tests are strong.

Each row records correctness/security (`C`), memory/concurrency/integer/resource safety (`S`), vSRX feature parity (`V`), performance/modularity (`P/M`), and tests or residual gaps (`T`).

| `userspace-dp/src/afxdp/icmp_embed/nat_match_v4.rs` | **C/S:** Traced embedded IPv4 options/fragments through session, static/NAT reversal and checksum updates; all local reads are checked and network-endian, with no unsafe ownership. **V/P/M/T:** Cold ICMP-exception logic is factored cleanly and allocation-free. The inner declared-length-versus-physical-quote concern is the existing `#2361` invariant, so it was suppressed; existing tests cover direction and checksum bytes. No new finding. |
| `userspace-dp/src/afxdp/icmp_embed/nat_match_v6.rs` | **C/S:** Traced IPv6 extension walking, NPTv6 reverse matching, session lookup and bounds; checked extension caps, fragments, endian and slice construction. **V/P/M/T:** Cold path, no added lock/allocation, and clean split from translation. NPT zone and embedded NAT64-PAT residuals map to prior audit canonicals; no new finding survived. |
| `userspace-dp/src/afxdp/poll_descriptor/nat_exception.rs` | **C/S:** Followed AF_XDP metadata/frame length into embedded-ICMP NAT exception, static fallback, drop/forward status, descriptor outcome and counters; no raw pointer or recycle transfer occurs here. **V/P/M/T:** Exception-only work is off the ordinary warmed path. Caller contracts and malformed/truncated outcomes are tested; application-match omission is upstream and reported in A2-b1-03. |
| `userspace-dp/src/nat/allocator.rs` | **C/S:** Audited bitmap geometry, `u16/u32/usize` conversions, AcqRel claim/Release free, mutex-protected live maps, persistent expiry indexes, deterministic blocks, recycle order, HA reserve and teardown. **V/P/M/T:** New-flow locks and atomics are intentional; status scans remain cold. Refused HA reservations lose transaction status (A2-b1-01), while address-only users have no ownership token (A2-b1-02). Stress tests cover successful claims/churn but not those orderings. |
| `userspace-dp/src/nat/destination.rs` | **C/S:** Checked parsing, address-family gates, LPM/protocol/port/application/ICMP constraints, static merge, counter ownership and malformed input. No unsafe or shared mutable hot state. **V/P/M/T:** Hash/LPM lookup is efficient and modular; configured first-match precedence is the audit-177 canonical and was suppressed. Tests are broad on bytes/decisions but intentionally encode the prior precedence. No new finding. |
| `userspace-dp/src/nat/mod.rs` | **C/S:** Reviewed decision composition, scope contracts, counter atomics and reset registry locking; Relaxed counters are telemetry, and reset is serialized. **V/P/M/T:** Public module boundaries are coherent; no warmed-path formatting/syscall was introduced. Counter tests cover clear/add races. No new finding. |
| `userspace-dp/src/nat/source.rs` | **C/S:** Traced parser, ordered scope/application match, interface/pool/deterministic allocation, ICMP identifiers, release and HA reserve across v4/v6; checked mutex/bitmap ownership and failure returns. **V/P/M/T:** A2-b1-01, A2-b1-02 and A2-b1-03 survive. Existing tests cover protocol/ports and successful lifecycle, but omit reserve refusal, address-only collision, and source-NAT ICMP type/code. |
| `userspace-dp/src/nat/static_nat.rs` | **C/S:** Checked host/block prefix arithmetic, source/scope constraints, port pairing and bidirectional translation; checked masks/shifts and no unsafe/shared mutation. **V/P/M/T:** Lookup remains allocation-free. Invalid-port wildcard/demotion behavior is already canonical in audit-177; tests cover offsets, ports, scopes and failures. No new finding. |
| `userspace-dp/src/nat/status.rs` | **C/S:** Reviewed allocator snapshots, aggregation and integer widening; no ownership transfer, and counters cannot affect forwarding. **V/P/M/T:** Bitmap popcount/map aggregation is status-path work rather than packet-path work; modular and covered by pool status tests. No new finding. |
| `userspace-dp/src/nat/tests_counter.rs` | **C/S:** Tests exercise concurrent clear-versus-hit, stable IDs, store sharing and zero-ID handling; assertions check exact counts. **V/P/M/T:** No runtime surface or hot-path overhead. Wrap is telemetry-only and no correctness candidate survived. |
| `userspace-dp/src/nat/tests_destination.rs` | **C/S:** Read every DNAT decision/source-scope/prefix/protocol/port/ICMP assertion for destination and failure status. **V/P/M/T:** Good broad parity coverage, but several tests codify specificity rather than config-order semantics already retained by audit-177. No distinct gap retained. |
| `userspace-dp/src/nat/tests_dnat_proto.rs` | **C/S:** Tests validate GRE, ICMPv6, HOPOPT-versus-wildcard and malformed protocol behavior with exact decisions. **V/P/M/T:** No production resource surface; useful protocol parity coverage. No new finding. |
| `userspace-dp/src/nat/tests_l4_match.rs` | **C/S:** Tests adversarially cover source/destination ports, never sentinels, unknown tuples, DNAT ICMP type/code and rule outcomes. **V/P/M/T:** The asymmetry is material: DNAT has ICMP constraints while source NAT tests only protocol/ports, corroborating A2-b1-03. |
| `userspace-dp/src/nat/tests_pool.rs` | **C/S:** Read allocation capacity, collision probing, persistent lease/GC, release/rollback, deterministic, concurrent fill/churn and HA reserve assertions. **V/P/M/T:** Strong lifecycle/perf coverage, but address-only tests assert zero ownership and HA tests only successful reservation; missing hostile cases support A2-b1-01 and A2-b1-02. |
| `userspace-dp/src/nat/tests_scope.rs` | **C/S:** Checked interface/zone/VRF and static/source constraints for both families and exact negative outcomes. **V/P/M/T:** No runtime safety surface; coverage is focused and modular. NPTv6 `from_zone` loss is a prior audit-177 canonical outside this test contract. No new finding. |
| `userspace-dp/src/nat/tests_source.rs` | **C/S:** Tests cover v4/v6 source/destination prefixes, malformed fail-closed behavior, off rules, reverse decisions and parse-error accounting. **V/P/M/T:** They do not construct ICMP type/code application terms, the A2-b1-03 gap; otherwise no distinct candidate. |
| `userspace-dp/src/nat/tests_static.rs` | **C/S:** Tests assert exact bidirectional addresses/ports, block offsets, host masks, invalid input and parse counters. **V/P/M/T:** No production concurrency/perf surface. Previously reported mapped-port and malformed-field behaviors were deduplicated; no new finding. |
| `userspace-dp/src/nat64.rs` | **C/S:** Traced v6 extension chains/fragments and declared lengths through BIB allocation, v6/v4 frame sizing, ICMP conversion, checksums, traffic class, HA reserve/release and output buffers; checked arithmetic and caller-owned buffers. **V/P/M/T:** Streaming checksum avoids per-packet vectors. Refused synced reserve is A2-b1-01; fragment association and embedded PAT quote issues are prior canonicals. |
| `userspace-dp/src/nat64_tests.rs` | **C/S:** Read byte-identical frame, checksum, padding trim, extension, fragment, ICMP, allocation, config reload and HA tests. Assertions generally verify bytes/status/checksums, and the low-level test proves a second owner is refused. **V/P/M/T:** No high-level test checks that such refusal aborts or rolls back sync, which is A2-b1-01. |
| `userspace-dp/src/nptv6.rs` | **C/S:** Checked `/48`/`/64` parsing, host-bit rejection, overlap, one-complement adjustment, `0xffff` representation, family/scope and prefix reconstruction; no unsafe/shared mutable state. **V/P/M/T:** Translation is allocation-free and modular. Missing `from_zone` is already an audit-177 canonical; no new finding. |
| `userspace-dp/src/nptv6_tests.rs` | **C/S:** Tests verify round trips, checksum neutrality, zero representations, invalid/overlapping snapshots and DNAT composition. **V/P/M/T:** Exact address outcomes are asserted; zone parity cannot be tested because the current wire omits it, already covered by the prior canonical. No new finding. |
| `userspace-dp/src/protocol/nat.rs` | **C/S:** Audited serde defaults, field widths and Go/Rust wire skew for all NAT families; no pointer/concurrency surface. **V/P/M/T:** Source-NAT application wire omits ICMP type/code while DNAT carries them (A2-b1-03). Additive defaults can preserve decode compatibility without packet-path allocation. |

| AST, edit, formatting, groups, redaction | Edit/group merge and inactive behavior are guarded; the retained archival-password omission violates the stated all-secret display invariant. | Clone ownership is sound and formatting is read-only; prior apply-groups recursion/resource and formatter duplicate-key roots were deduplicated. | Formatting is linear over the tree in normal use; redaction is intended to match Junos `SECRET-DATA`. | Secret classification is centralized, but its hand-maintained inventory omitted an existing password-bearing grammar and its test vector. |
| Compiler pipeline and dispatch | Strict-versus-lenient gates generally preserve fail-closed commit behavior without bricking stored/peer configs. | No shared mutable compiler state was found; bounded range expansion is generally present. Prior section-hard-error and recursion findings were deduplicated. | Three-phase compile ordering and per-node derivation are explicit; no new latency issue survived. | Uniform gates are modular, though open-world grammar remains the existing `#4313` root rather than a new finding. |
| Applications and AppID | Application/set references, term shape, protocol/port/ICMP constraints, collisions, and nested-set failures are validated. | Port parsing is bounded; recursive set expansion has a depth guard. | Named-port and Junos alias parity are covered; no new per-packet cost was introduced here. | Tests are broad across flat/hierarchical shapes; no new AppID residual survived dedup. |
| Chassis and interfaces | Device-map uniqueness, interface-range expansion, unsupported knobs, and typed tunnel widths were checked. | Tunnel integer widths are schema-bounded; the MaxInt interface-range loop is real but exactly deduplicated to `#4807`. | Accepted-but-inert knobs carry advisories; range expansion is bounded in normal validated inputs. | Tests cover malformed ranges and unsupported interface stanzas; no new root retained. |
| CoS and firewall | Family-any, filter references/actions/protocols, code-point bounds, and queue bijection gates are fail-closed. | Percent conversion clamps at `MaxUint64`; bounded queue/code-point domains avoid wire truncation. | Accepted-but-inert CoS behavior is warned; prior unknown symbolic code-point and CoS parity findings were deduplicated. | Firewall match/action allowlists are explicit and well tested; no distinct new issue survived. |
| DDNS and DHCP | Credential transport, malformed endpoints/durations, relay overrides, and TSIG display behavior were checked. | No unbounded expansion or shared-state issue was found in assigned paths. | Backend advisories expose unsupported behavior; literal DDNS userinfo falls under the existing `#4861` fix locus. | Provider tests are broad; archival-password redaction remains outside the DDNS-focused secret vector. |
| IPsec | Proposal/policy/gateway/selector gates are mostly strict; invalid bind-interface strings are the retained commit/runtime gap. | XFRM IDs use bounded 16-bit components packed into `uint32`; invalid input maps to sentinel zero and causes no netlink allocation. | A green commit followed by an absent xfrmi is below vSRX commit-check behavior; runtime logging is not a substitute. | Collision tests cover `stN`/`stN.0`, but no test covers a single unparsable bind-interface. |
| NAT and NPTv6 | Address, application, port, scope, target, prefix, and overlap checks were traced through strict and lenient paths. | Valid port expansion is bounded; full-domain IPv4 count wrap and oversized range roots are already catalogued. | Accepted routing-instance/overloading knobs warn; no distinct parity or hot-path regression survived. | Dual-AST and duplicate-block coverage is extensive; open-world match typo behavior is the existing `#4313` root. |
| Security policy | Required dimensions, unsupported leaves, address/application resolution, duplicate blocks, global zones, actions, and logs are gated. | Walks are bounded by AST size and do not retain mutable global state. | Unsupported vSRX L7 dimensions reject rather than widen; no compiler hot-path issue found. | Allowlist and compiler switch are currently aligned and have flat/hierarchical/lenient coverage. |

The two cluster commands completed in under ten seconds before the coordinator's explicit timeout checkpoint; every subsequent test/check command was wrapped in the requested five-minute bound.
- Limitations: no live or destructive cluster tests were run. Package-level output does not enumerate privileged `CAP_NET_RAW` skips, so passing socket tests do not prove behavior on every kernel/driver/VRF combination. Timing findings were established from control flow and fixed deadlines rather than a live multi-target outage. vSRX parity for global IP-monitoring threshold semantics was checked against the Juniper CLI reference.

##### Module-by-module inspection log

###### Cluster

Across the cluster module I checked correctness/security of election, heartbeat authentication/replay/family validation, readiness, monitor debt, GARP failover, sync authentication/framing/bulk/config/failover, and status reporting. Memory/concurrency/resource checks covered lock order, atomic generations, timer/goroutine ownership, socket and listener shutdown, frame length/endian handling, and bounded queues. vSRX parity checks covered monitor weighting and HA state behavior. Performance checks covered polling, handshake acceptance, logging, and retry paths. Module boundaries were checked through direct manager, daemon callback, config, dataplane, and VRRP contracts. Existing tests are broad, but the surviving gaps are the threshold model, bulk transaction validity, serial probe latency, and pre-auth admission bound described below.

###### Conntrack

The conntrack sweep covered expiration correctness, companion and PNAT deletion, adaptive GC cadence, per-IP count accounting, atomics, and dataplane ownership. Production userspace startup sets legacy sweeping off while Rust owns session expiry, so legacy-only observations were weighted by reachability. No security, memory, integer, resource, parity, performance, modularity, or test-gap candidate survived as a fresh actionable root; package and race tests passed.

| Exact path | Inspection result / invariant checked |
|---|---|
| `pkg/conntrack/gc.go` | Expiry and companion cleanup are bounded and key/value copies have clear ownership. A possible stale count-map concern is not consumed by the active BPF path and production disables the legacy sweep, so it does not survive as a reportable defect. |
| `pkg/conntrack/gc_test.go` | Covers expiry, companions, PNAT, adaptive timing, and counters; tests agree with the reachable legacy contract. |
| `pkg/conntrack/legacy_dataplane_canary_test.go` | Canary explicitly guards the dormant legacy dataplane assumption; no feature-parity claim beyond that boundary survived. |

###### Router advertisements

The RA sweep covered config reconciliation, per-interface epochs/tombstones, owner-goroutine serialization, timer lifecycle, RS source/hop-limit/type validation, ICMPv6 marshal/checksum behavior, link-local source selection, lifetime semantics, and write ordering. Locks/channels/timers are generally ownership-clean and test/race runs passed. The surviving day-2 feature/correctness gap is stale interface MAC metadata after RETH reprogramming (A5-b1-05); prior goodbye and global-epoch findings were deduplicated.

##### Module-by-module inspection log

###### `pkg/dataplane`

Dimension coverage: correctness/security included fail-closed mutation ordering, map-key/value ABI, session companion and NAT alias ownership; safety included lock ownership, native/network byte order, width/alignment, generation wrap, iterator errors, allocation bounds, and syscall count; vSRX parity included NAT, proxy ARP/NDP, filter expansion, counters, and clear behavior; performance included batch map operations and 10M-entry capacity; modularity included runtime-domain adapters and retirement boundaries; tests were checked for success, partial failure, rollback, race, and scale gaps. Rows marked Sound state the checked invariant and why no candidate survived.

| `pkg/dataplane/zone_flood_counters_hide_test.go` | Correctness/security: stable-hash IDs no longer index legacy dense arrays, invalid direction is rejected by the callee, and populated zero is distinct from unavailable. The serial setter/clear test misses a current cross-generation/racing publication defect in the shipped zone-traffic path (A6-b3-04). Memory/concurrency/integer/resource: the sparse maps are `uint16` keyed and mutex protected, but per-row mutation does not provide snapshot retirement; map size is bounded by configured zones. vSRX completeness: per-zone traffic is shipped; per-zone flood counters remain explicitly deferred under open `#3651`, so that known parity gap was deduplicated rather than re-reported. Performance/latency: publication is a 1 Hz control-plane path, not packet path; an atomic map replacement is acceptable. Modularity/test gaps: the assigned test still describes both families as HIDE-only and tests the shim map in isolation rather than the userspace-manager publication transaction. |
| `pkg/dataplane/zoneid_stable_test.go` | Correctness/security: add/remove stability and equality with `config.StableZoneID` are correctly pinned; the hash range excludes 0 and reserved IDs, while strict collision rejection and lenient quarantine are covered in `pkg/config`. The local reverse helper and many direct `ApplyResult` consumers still choose an arbitrary colliding name (A6-b3-05). Memory/concurrency/integer/resource: compile-time map work is bounded; `uint16` folding and reserved-range arithmetic are sound; no shared-memory or packet-path concurrency is involved. vSRX completeness: ordinary zone identity is stable, but lenient degraded-mode session/zone naming can contradict the surviving runtime zone. Performance/latency: hashing and reverse-map construction are apply/operator cold paths. Modularity/test gaps: reverse ownership should be a single production helper/map rather than repeated map iteration; the assigned fixtures never use the frozen colliding pair. |

</details>

###### Module risk coverage

- **Daemon:** checked host-account ownership/revocation, rename and `.link` persistence, HA RG state ordering, runtime interface contracts, RSS queue bounds/idempotence, command/file resource handling, and test seams. Mutex/atomic state in RG code and command timeouts appeared coherent; surviving defects are credential error-state loss and an RSS completeness check.
- **FRR:** checked managed-file ownership/atomicity, reload serialization and retry generations, command injection guards, route-map semantics, BGP hierarchy, status parsing, route rendering, and configuration-build cost. No memory/concurrency defect survived; two vSRX/FRR semantic mismatches survive because textual tests do not validate loaded route-map behavior.
- **IPsec:** checked secret decoding, proposal/token mappings, resolver concurrency bounds, render escaping, reload/state promotion, SA deletion, XFRM identifiers, and error/resource lifetimes. Manager locking and bounded subprocess execution appeared sound; termination ownership and DH-group mapping defects survive.
- **networkd:** checked protected-file ownership, atomic write/remove accounting, activation debt, reconfigure debt, sysctl restoration, generated unit safety, and empty-set cleanup. The mutexed Apply debt is sound, but the separate Clear path does not carry reload debt.
- **Routing:** checked per-domain locks, netlink object ownership, teardown retry, rule priority/window bounds, route family/endian handling, tunnel generation atomics and goroutine drain, ICMP nonce/sequence wrap, stable no-churn reconciliation, and display/test coverage. No race or integer/alignment defect survived race/vet; error propagation and bond member activation gaps remain. Existing route-display and HA-monitor roots were deduplicated.

## Findings by Confidence
